assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit, read end to end with its front matter: the canonical V2 individual character monograph series/lycoris-recoil/03 V2 Working Artifacts/05 Specialist Synthesis/LYCORIS_RECOIL_MIZUKI_CHARACTER_SYNTHESIS.md (31,058 bytes, status canonical, empty supersession arrays, veto false), a portrait of Nakahara Mizuki in the Japanese TV series (E01-E13) and the six Friends are thieves of time shorts. It locates her by episode and timecode, cue and frame, and by the project's claim and behaviour IDs (CLM, MIZ-MB). It closes with 'A conditional portrait', which states what she is likely to do and what it leaves untested. The discovery row claims E01-E13 and Shorts 01-06 and does not claim speech. The portrait's prose (Ordinary days, Recovery days), Recollect and anthology sections are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity, and no prediction here rests on them. The source inventory, ledgers, claim matrices and crosswalk it links are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them directly. The project's COMPLETE_AT_BOUNDARY outcome was not adopted as a grade. No primary source was inspected for this assessment.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Her history belongs to her at every state, so far as the portrait gives it: intelligence work at DA, whose duties, timing and experiences are largely unshown, and the motive she gives for leaving (E01); and the time when LilyBell came to the shop to kill Chisato and Mika and Kusunoki negotiated with their superiors, which she recalls (E12). Located present states: introduction, the restaurant review and the Cleaner's cost (E01); playing Walnut in the staged death for triple pay (E02); the museum field operation, being disabled and returning to relay findings (E05); the rock-paper-scissors fix, the extraction drive and the blame for the breach (E06); the structural danger to the branch (E07); the rush (E08); driving Chisato to DA (E09); the closure and the Vancouver prospect (E10); the airport and the recall (E11); the LilyBell history and the helicopter (E12); and the Hawaii coda (E13). The shorts are placed as the portrait places them, without a calendar. Nothing after E13; print stories are outside scope.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution) and the owner's A/B boundary direction of 24 November 2026 in PR #694, not yet recorded in the policy: A turns on the integration, individuation and transferability of the model within a declared scope; interpretations that predict the same behavior may coexist; divergent transfer conditions, missing evidence and unsettled dispositions are named and excluded rather than counted against the tier; held-out validation, analytical derivation, relationship labels and preserved source chronology are not barriers. Evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: 'A conditional portrait' gives an organizing pattern: she notices what someone else's plan leaves out, such as a cost, a credible response in the field or a flight-time limit, and says so first and sharply (E01 Cleaner, E06 rock-paper-scissors, E07 the branch's dependence, E12 time in the air). It also makes narrow predictions. A known colleague's risky favor draws a question about how it will work or who pays. In conflict she infers blame too quickly, and the injured person's own account can matter more (E06). As the stakes and the credibility of a specific person's need rise, concrete service becomes more likely, with complaint (E05, E11-E12). In low-stakes leisure, romance or a beer can be reason enough to prefer her own plan (E10, Shorts). It predicts her mistakes: folding causal contribution into blame (E06), deciding how much friends should know to get natural reactions (E02), and enjoying an unwitting performance she would object to as snooping (E07, Short 04). Not B: the hinge of the account is when a known person's need outweighs pay, leisure or romance, and that is shown in one configuration. In E11 Kurumi supplies the stake and the direction. The portrait says Mizuki's own feelings there are less accessible, and that the scene gives few grounds to say whether she needed pressure or had planned to return. Her E02 risk is given in her own terms as pay. The portrait names as untested what she would do if a relationship and a costly claim could both be kept. The evidence does not establish which motive decides outside that one configuration, which is insufficiency, not productive uncertainty. Not D: the cost-first objection, the hasty blame and helping while complaining are located conditional patterns across E01-E12.

Located states: the former intelligence worker with a stated motive for leaving (E01), the cafe adult and field support (E01-E09), the closure and a plan of her own (E10), the trip given up (E11), and the flight in the rescue (E12). The portrait says her willingness to help becomes more visible once she knows the stake. Not B: it declines to read this as moral improvement ('It does not establish ... every mistake a step in moral improvement'); there is no located inner transition; her DA years are largely unshown. Not D: the states are located by episode and the portrait separates visibility from change.

Located forms only: キモい for DA (E01); おっさん for Mika (E01, E12); ガキンチョ and other talking-down to Kurumi; バッチコ～イ (E12); 'goodbye, darling' (E11); 'I'm still in my twenties' as a drunken protest (Short 04); a comic 'I don't speak English' and a reassurance in Japanese to a client (E13); and the closing summary of familiar address, nominal assertions about what people ought to do and an occasional exasperated ending. Not C: the discovery row says speech is thin and does not claim it; the portrait gives no register rules and defers vocal quality to separate audiovisual evidence. Not E: several individuated forms recur with named listeners.

Ordinary life is located across TV and shorts: claiming the restaurant review and the contest over who is cute (E01); the mother-talent joke to the television (E01); beer after the costume (E02); the rush and the phone (E08); the Vancouver prospect from a matchmaking site (E10); sleeping on the plane (E11); drinking and singing (Short 01); dessert judgments and the cost record (Short 03); taking the shop's alcohol home and the mutual silence with Chisato (Short 04); 'Aloha' and vacation clothes (Short 06); the Hawaii client (E13). Not A: her home, dating encounters and life away from the cafe are not shown, and the portrait warns against diagnosing addiction from parties. Not C: the routines recur and are located across many episodes and shorts.

Directed differences: Kurumi has the widest range (risk for her in E02, wanting her on the ground in E05, blaming her in E06, ガキンチョ, the mutual airport admission, being commandeered in E11, sharing the rescue in E12); Chisato (teasing, accompanying her to DA without claiming access to hidden distress in E09, deciding what she should know in E02, mutual blackmail in Short 04); Mika (おっさん, asking why and how much, shared work in E08); Takina (a strategy against Chisato's game, speaking for her in E06 in a way she does not share, history and social judgment in Short 03); strangers (a client reassured in Japanese, E13). Not A: her DA colleagues, Kusunoki and her romantic prospects are offstage. Not C: each relationship has located states and a stated difference.

Stated motives only: sick of the organization that makes orphans into killers (E01); good pay worth the risk (E02); losing the shop would remove a place to meet men (E07). The portrait states directly that her own feelings are less accessible at the airport. Not C: there is no inner monologue, few self-explanations, and the portrait declines to read her feelings at the scene that matters most. Not E: the stated motives are located.

Located modes: objecting to the Cleaner's expense, then exasperation rather than argument (E01); grouping consequences as blame and urging Takina to speak (E06); objecting to reading another's phone while explaining the structural danger (E07); turning an accusation into a negotiation for silence (Short 04); complying while telling Kurumi to stop ordering her around (E11). Not B: no conflict tests her limits, and the portrait leaves her limit on justified force untested. Not D: the modes are varied and located with outcomes.

Located positions: disgust at DA making orphans into killers (E01); the Cleaner's cost (E01); natural reactions as a reason to keep the girls uninformed (E02); blame for the breach (E06); objection to snooping (E07). Not C: she is never shown weighing alternatives in the continuity, and her one sustained moral objection is in print (Ordinary days), outside scope. Not E: several positions are located against her acts.

Humor is a recurrent mode with located functions: claiming the review (E01); the mother-talent protest at the television (E01); the recording she teases Chisato with (E02); 'goodbye, darling' (E11); 'sinners' and the negotiated silence (Short 04); valuing the 'good voice' the prank produced (Short 04); laughing at Mika's vacation readiness (Short 06); 'I don't speak English' (E13). Not A: the portrait does not say when her teasing yields, and it warns that not every sharp line is affectionate. Not C: the instances are many, located and their function described.

One dedicated portrait covers E01-E13 and the six shorts with timecodes, cues, frames and claim and behaviour IDs, and separates continuity evidence from attributed print. Not A: the row curates only this derived item, the ledgers behind it are not on the row, and exact vocal quality and continuous action are deferred to separate audiovisual evidence. Not C: each major appearance and decision is located.

Located bounds against overreading: her E09 remark that Chisato is behaving as usual grants no access to hidden distress; parties and jokes give no diagnosis of addiction (Short 01); 'in my twenties' gives no birth date and her English is unknown (Short 04, E13); the E02 remark about the unused fallback and the E06 escalation line and apology have unmarked speakers; piloting gives no credential history (E12); she did not author the earlier LilyBell negotiation (E12); the mother-talent joke is no tested plan (E01); Kurumi's credit 'even in death' is not fact (E05); her E07 forecast about the branch is defeasible; and there are few grounds to say she wanted pressure or had planned to return (E11). Not A: no forecast about her is tested against later evidence. Not C: each bound is located.

States are placed by episode and timecode. Not B: there is no story calendar, her DA period and the LilyBell history are undated, and the shorts are undated. Not D: the episode states are precisely located.

scenario_readiness.note: The discovery row does not claim speech. The portrait gives located forms but no register rules, and defers vocal quality to separate audiovisual evidence. Generated lines would be constrained by content, not by a source-supported voice.

conditions: A known colleague proposes a risky or costly course: predict a question about how it will actually work or who bears the expense (E01, E07).
A plan leaves out a practical element: predict that she names it first and sharply, such as a cost, a better tactic or a time limit (E01, E06, E12).
A friend has been harmed by someone in the group: predict a quick attribution of blame and an invitation to the injured person to speak; the injured person's own account may override hers (E06).
A job where friends' natural reactions are useful: predict that she may keep them uninformed and tease them with the result afterward (E02, Short 04).
Low-stakes leisure: predict that romance, travel or a drink can decide her preference (E10, Shorts 01 and 06).

Separate, lower-confidence condition: a cafe member's credible, high-stakes need, with the stake made clear to her. Predict compliance with complaint, even at the cost of a personal plan (E11-E12). This is observed once, with Kurumi supplying the stake and the direction.
Include her mistakes: hasty blame, deciding what others should know, and mockery of an unwitting performance.

Exclude what she would give up for an unfamiliar person, her limit on justified force, a choice where a relationship and a costly claim could both be kept, her DA intelligence work, any renewed DA role, and romance outcomes.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: Television E01-E13 and the shorts, with her DA service and the LilyBell history in the past at every state; from E10 the cafe is closed and she has a plan to leave; from E11 she has given up the trip for the rescue. Nothing after E13.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Kurumi, Chisato, Takina and Mika as colleagues at the cafe; cafe customers and a client in the Hawaii coda. A comparable new colleague is a separate, lower-confidence condition.
setting_constraints: Cafe LycoReco, field support and the television series' Tokyo, with DA as the series presents it.
No print or anthology scene, no account of her DA work beyond what is stated, and no outcome invented to settle a prediction.

scenario_readiness.note: Narrow extrapolation follows the portrait's conditional patterns within the cafe group. The decisive trade-off between a person's need and her own pay, leisure or romance is supported only in the E11 configuration.

conditions: Cafe and leisure settings with the staff and customers: serving, drinking and singing, teasing and negotiated silences, holiday plans, as in E01, E08 and Shorts 01, 03, 04 and 06.
Dating encounters, her home and life away from the cafe are not modeled.
scenario_readiness.note: Cafe life, leisure and ordinary company are located across the episodes and shorts.

Her positions are located, but she is never shown weighing alternatives in the continuity; her one sustained moral objection is a print scene outside scope. Reasoning in a new dilemma would be invented.

Her wish for romance recurs (E01, E07, E10, E11), but no partner, encounter or relationship is shown; the man in Vancouver is offstage and they are 'not dating yet'. A romance scenario would rest on invention.

conditions: Cafe work: serving and the phone in a rush, cost objections and practical allocation (E01, E08).
Field support for the group: observation and relay, a tracker, driving an extraction and flying a helicopter while stating its time limit (E05, E06, E12).
Excluded: her DA intelligence duties, any credentials, Kurumi's technical information work, and performance beyond the located task.
scenario_readiness.note: Her cafe and field-support work is located; her DA intelligence career is not.

known_limits.statement: The portrait states that her own feelings are less accessible than her judgments, notably at the airport, where resignation, room for another's regret, anticipation and reluctance coexist.

The trip she gives up in E11 is the one depicted case of a friend's need overriding a personal plan. Kurumi supplies the stake and the direction, and the portrait gives few grounds to say whether pressure was needed or she had planned to return.
Her DA intelligence duties, timing and experiences are largely unshown, and her piloting gives no credential history.
The E02 remark about the unused fallback and the E06 escalation line and apology have unmarked or separately attributed speakers, and no prediction rests on them.
Her drinking is located in parties and jokes, and the portrait warns against diagnosing addiction or reading sobriety from them.
The discovery row does not claim speech, and the portrait defers vocal quality and continuous action to separate audiovisual evidence.
Prose, Recollect and anthology scenes, including her objection to waiting in Ordinary days, are attributed comparisons outside the television continuity and are not used for prediction.
Untested: what she would give up for an unfamiliar person, her limit on justified force, and her choice where a relationship and a costly claim on her could both be kept.
There is no evidence of her conduct after E13.
